title: App Review Guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Last updated 16 October 2026. 2.1(a) demo account and live back end; 2.3.1(a) specific review notes; 2.5.2 no downloaded code that changes functionality; 4.2 minimum functionality; 4.8 equivalent login option; 5.1.1 privacy policy, purpose strings, in-app account deletion; 5.1.2 App Tracking Transparency; 3.1.1 in-app purchase and the 3.1.1(a) US storefront link exception; 1.3 Kids Category.

title: Upcoming requirements
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Since 28 April 2026 uploads must be built with Xcode 26 and the 26 SDKs; since 9 September 2026 iOS and iPadOS apps must target iOS 13 or later; age rating answers due 31 January 2026; approved reasons for listed APIs, including in third-party SDKs, since 1 May 2024; apps without DSA trader status removed from the EU App Store since 17 February 2025.

title: App privacy details on the App Store
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Declare all data you and third-party partners (including SDKs) collect; definitions of collect, linked to the user and tracking; narrow optional-disclosure criteria; answers can be updated at any time without an app update.

title: App Review
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Typically at least 50% of submissions reviewed in under 24 hours and 90% in under 48 hours; expedited review for critical bug fixes with steps to reproduce; one appeal per rejected submission; demo account in App Review Information.

title: Release a version update in phases
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Phased release over 7 days at 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100% of users with automatic updates; anyone can still update manually; pause up to 30 days in total; Release to All Users at any time; removing the app from sale ends the phased release.

title: TestFlight overview
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Up to 100 internal testers and 10,000 external testers; the first build added to an external group goes to review; builds can be tested for up to 90 days.

title: Offering account deletion in your app
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Deletion must start in the app; a direct link to a web page is allowed; no phone or email flows outside highly regulated industries; revoke Sign in with Apple tokens; explain subscriptions continue until cancelled; tell people how long deletion takes.

title: Manage European Union Digital Services Act trader requirements
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Every developer declares trader status; verified address, phone and email show on the EU product page; verification by two-factor codes and documents; Apple suggests a legal adviser if unsure.

title: Overview of Accessibility Nutrition Labels
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Nine features can be declared (VoiceOver, Voice Control, Larger Text, Dark Interface, Differentiate Without Color Alone, Sufficient Contrast, Reduced Motion, Captions, Audio Descriptions); voluntary for now, required later; claim a feature only if all common tasks work with it.

title: UI Design Dos and Don'ts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Controls at least 44 x 44 points; text at least 11 points; ample contrast between text and background.

title: Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section
supports: Opened with WebFetch. All apps on closed, open or production tracks complete the form, even with no data collected; internal-testing-only apps exempt; developers answer for SDKs; ephemeral processing; Google does not verify answers and may block updates or remove apps for misrepresentation.

title: Target API level requirements for Google Play apps
supports: Opened with WebFetch. From 31 August 2026 new apps and updates must target Android 16 (API 36); existing apps must target Android 15 (API 35) to stay discoverable to new users on newer Android versions; extension available to 1 November 2026.

title: Set up an open, closed or internal test
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Internal testing up to 100 testers, available within minutes, may skip standard reviews; closed lists up to 2,000 testers each or Google Groups; open testing unlimited or a limit of at least 1,000; test links can take several hours.

title: Release app updates with staged rollouts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Rollout percentage does not rise on its own; halt stops new users getting the version, people who have it keep it; resume only if the bundle is fine; updates only, not first publication; countries cannot be removed once a staged rollout starts.

title: App testing requirements for new personal developer accounts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Personal accounts created after 13 November 2023 need a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for the last 14 days in a row before applying for production; review usually within 7 days.

title: Understanding Google Play's app account deletion requirements
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Apps that let users create accounts need an in-app deletion path and a web link; declared in the Data safety form; retention reasons must be disclosed; enforcement possible after 31 May 2024.

title: Support 16 KB page sizes
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Apps targeting Android 15 and higher must support 16 KB pages on 64-bit devices on Google Play; from 1 February 2027 updates without support cannot be released; Java and Kotlin-only apps already comply; check .so files with APK Analyzer; AGP 8.5.1+ and NDK r28+ align by default.

title: Android vitals
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Bad behaviour thresholds: user-perceived crash rate 1.09% overall and 8% per phone model; ANR rate 0.47% overall and 8% per phone model; excessive partial wake locks 5%; Play may reduce visibility and warn on the listing; 28-day window; memory thresholds may affect visibility from February 2027; vitals rates are per daily active user, Crashlytics per session.

title: Android developer verification
supports: Opened with WebFetch. From 30 September 2026 protections apply to installs from participating stores in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand on certified devices running Android 7+; global expansion in 2027; Google Play registers 99% of apps automatically.

title: Display content edge-to-edge in views
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Apps targeting SDK 35 are drawn edge-to-edge on Android 15 and higher; handle system bar, display cutout and gesture insets so content is not hidden.

title: Touch target size
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Touch targets at least 48 x 48 dp, separated by 8 dp of space or more.

title: Build an offline-first app
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Local data source as source of truth; show local data at once; online-only, queued and lazy writes; exponential backoff without retrying unauthorised requests; pull and push sync; last write wins.

title: React Native blog
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 0.88 released 19 October 2026; 0.86 (11 June 2026) edge-to-edge improvements; 0.84 (11 February 2026) Hermes V1 by default; 0.82 (8 October 2025) the first version to run entirely on the New Architecture.

title: Expo SDK reference: versions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Expo SDK 58 uses React Native 0.88 and React 19.3.0; supports Android 7+ and iOS 16.4+; needs Xcode 26.4+; target SDK 36, compile SDK 37.

title: Flutter release notes
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Newest stable line listed is 3.47 (after 3.44, 3.41 and 3.38); a notice says 3.47.8 blocks compromised eMudhra CA keys. No release dates on the page.

title: Accessibility
supports: Opened with WebFetch. accessible, accessibilityLabel, accessibilityHint, accessibilityRole, accessibilityState, live regions and aria-* equivalents; TalkBack always reads hints, VoiceOver only if the user turned hints on.

title: Suddenly FBSDKRestrictiveDataFilterManager.m - Line 71 started to crash (issue 1373)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Opened 6 May 2020: apps with the Facebook iOS SDK crashed at launch without an app change; Meta said on 7 May a release on its side triggered the crashes and it was fixed; issue closed 7 May 2020.

title: React Native is the Future of Mobile at Shopify
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 29 January 2020: Shopify builds all new mobile apps in React Native; existing apps not automatically rewritten; expected about 80% code sharing, reached 95% in Arrive and 99% in Compass.

title: European accessibility act
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Covers products and services including smartphones, e-commerce, banking services, e-books and passenger transport services; member states had to transpose it by June 2022. The page does not mention apps by name.

title: Code of practice for app store operators and app developers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. First published 9 December 2022, updated version 13 October 2023, implementation period extended to June 2024; sets minimum security and privacy requirements for app stores and developers.
